concepts.def: Sex is biological (chromosomes, anatomy); gender is socially constructed identity and roles.
Typical female sex chromosomes are XX, male are XY; SRY gene on Y triggers testis development.
Klinefelter's (XXY) and Turner's (XO) syndromes provide insight into chromosomal effects on gender behaviour.
Gender identity (2-3), gender stability (4-5), gender constancy (6-7); children seek same-gender models after constancy.
Martin and Halverson (1981): once children acquire gender identity (age 2-3), they organise behaviour around gender schemas.
Bandura: gender behaviours learned through observation and reinforcement of same-sex models.
